claims.text: A defect-inclusive ML interatomic potential can predict the thermal conductivity of bulk HfNbTaTiZr containing 1 wt.% oxygen across 0–200 K and 300–1200 K.
The ML-IAP will improve thermal-conductivity prediction accuracy by at least 30% relative to conventional perfect-crystal analytical models.
Oxygen is initially randomly distributed in the modeled HfNbTaTiZr specimen.
The modeled specimen contains intrinsic vacancy defects.
Randomly distributed oxygen and intrinsic vacancies mimic realistic imperfect HfNbTaTiZr microstructures.
The proposed DFT training data explicitly include oxygen substitutions, oxygen interstitials, and vacancies in HfNbTaTiZr.
Static-defect phonon scattering dominates thermal transport in the 0–200 K regime.
Anharmonic phonon–phonon interactions become prominent in the 300–1200 K regime.
Oxygen-related point defects and vacancies perturb local bonding in HfNbTaTiZr.
Oxygen-related point defects and vacancies perturb the phonon spectra of HfNbTaTiZr.
Training on a wide range of defect configurations enables the ML-IAP to capture enhanced low-temperature phonon scattering caused by defects.
The ML-IAP captures the influence of high-temperature anharmonic interactions.
Detailed defect modeling more closely reproduces experimental vibrational behavior and thereby reduces thermal-conductivity prediction errors.
A held-out thermal-conductivity benchmark near 100 K is approximately 4 W/(mK).
Conventional perfect-crystal analytical models fail to adequately capture defect-induced scattering in oxygen-containing HfNbTaTiZr.
Conventional analytical predictions generally have errors of approximately 30% or more relative to experiment over the studied temperature ranges.
The proposed ML-IAP is applicable to bulk HfNbTaTiZr containing no more than 1 wt.% oxygen and to the temperature intervals 0–200 K and 300–1200 K.
Predictions outside the specified oxygen content, temperature ranges, or sampled defect configurations may not generalize reliably.
